title.value: On The Fragility of Learned Reward Functions
title.justification: The paper focuses on evaluating the stability and reliability of learned reward functions used in reinforcement learning.
title.quote: Our work focuses on demonstrating and studying the causes of these relearning failures in the domain of preference-based reward learning.

extractions.description: The paper studies the fragility and limitations of learned reward functions in reinforcement learning, particularly focusing on preference-based reward learning. It demonstrates how current methods can result in reward models that fail to train new agents from scratch, discusses factors affecting these failures, and emphasizes the need for retraining-based evaluations.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper is primarily about the technical evaluation and improvement of reward learning methods in reinforcement learning, with no explicit focus on sustainable development topics such as climate or ecological sustainability.

applications.value: Preference-based reward learning in reinforcement learning
applications.justification: The paper explores applications and limitations of preference-based reward learning in training AI models, though not in a context of sustainable development.
applications.quote: One of the most promising approaches is to learn reward functions from binary human preferences over trajectory segments where these segments are collected online.
